# OpenTimestamps fixtures

Bytes off the live wire, captured on 2026-09-10 and checked in verbatim. They
exist because the .ots format is not something this project defines: a parser
tested only against proofs this repository made up would be testing its own idea
of the format rather than the format.

Nothing here is regenerated by a script. To replace a file, capture it again and
say where from.

## The files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `anchor-2026-09-09.json` | `GET https://app.nomankind.ai/anchors/2026-09-09`, production's own anchor for that day, carrying the pending proof its calendar answered. |
| `calendar-upgraded.json` | `GET https://alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org/timestamp/<commitment>` — the 200, with the body base64 in `body_base64`. |
| `calendar-pending.json` | `GET https://a.pool.opentimestamps.org/timestamp/<commitment>` — the 404 the pool answered for the same commitment, body and all. |

## The chain these bytes make

```
anchor hash   sha256:555b1f1611e7ddccd60c33bf6d02dbbf27867099afa45742fcf41897c2750a8c
  (append and sha256, the calendar's nonces)
commitment    6aa1f3476dbb13ac82e5e673fa16dd08fc239afdfa890ccfd8a3ae42d6c19cdb386441334f1a3ae73a744392
  (the calendar's answer: its merkle path)
merkle root   7361cdb885061573576c8f74d14698b6b97096aa474f96e9202dd21d88e27617
  = the merkle root of Bitcoin block 966287
```

The last step was checked against a block explorer when these were captured:
`GET https://blockstream.info/api/block-height/966287` gives block
`0000000000000000000009167bf812e0619ce2cb6cd5b48d0691b6c3d1878721`, whose
`merkle_root` is `1776e2881dd22d20e9964f47aa9670b9b69846d1748f6c5773150685b8cd6173`
— the same 32 bytes, in the display order explorers reverse into. So the block
height in `test/anchor-upgrade.test.ts` is a fact about Bitcoin rather than a
number anyone here chose.

## Two calendars, on purpose

The receipt records `https://a.pool.opentimestamps.org`, which is the endpoint
the digest was posted to. The pool forwards to member calendars, and it does not
serve `/timestamp/` for a commitment one of them holds — on 2026-09-10 it
answered 404 for the very commitment `alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org`
answered 200 for. The calendar that can finish a proof is the one named inside
the proof's own pending attestation, which is why the adapter asks that one
first and the recorded one after. Both captures are here so that stays honest.
